title: The Baffling Case of the Body On Somerton Beach
summary: Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Matt) open with banter about the 2017 total solar eclipse, then tell the story of the Somerton Man, an unidentified well-dressed man found dead on Somerton Beach in Adelaide, South Australia, in 1948. They cover the initial sighting, autopsy findings, poison theories, his suitcase and personal effects, the Rubaiyat scrap of paper with the words "Tamam Shud," the phone number and code, the woman Jessica Thompson, Alfred Boxall, DNA testing linking him to Robin Thompson, exhumation attempts, and competing theories (suicide, espionage, murder). The episode closes with listener mail about New Jersey accents and an outro.

segments.title: Opening banter and eclipse talk
segments.summary: The hosts chat about the recent total solar eclipse, their experiences viewing it, and future eclipse plans, then transition to the Somerton Man case.

segments.title: Setting the scene: Adelaide and the discovery on the beach
segments.summary: Background on Adelaide's reputation for gruesome murders and post-war Australia, then the sighting of a well-dressed man on Somerton Beach on a Tuesday evening in November by jeweler John Lyons and his wife, and the next morning when he was found dead.

segments.title: Autopsy and poisoning theories
segments.summary: Autopsy findings including damaged organs and unusual pupils, the suspicion of poisoning, and the coroner's inquest where Cedric Stanton Hicks named digitalis and strophanthin, though no direct evidence of poisoning was ever found.

segments.title: Physical description and distinctive features
segments.summary: Description of the man's appearance, clothing, unusual calves, ear and teeth traits (hypodontia), and his lack of a hat.

segments.title: Personal effects and suitcase
segments.summary: Items found in his pockets (gum, matches, bus and train tickets, cigarettes), missing wallet and labels, the burial and plaster bust, and the suitcase left in a cloakroom with orange thread and American-style tie and stitching clues.

segments.title: Tamam Shud scrap of paper and the Rubaiyat
segments.summary: A scrap of paper reading Tamam Shud found in a hidden pocket leads to the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam; a copy is later found in a car, with a phone number and a coded message written inside.

segments.title: Jessica Thompson, Alfred Boxall and later DNA evidence
segments.summary: The phone number leads to nurse Jessica Thompson, who gave copies of the Rubaiyat to lovers including Alfred Boxall; her son Robin's features matched the Somerton Man, and DNA testing by Derek Abbott's side was pursued, with exhumation petitions denied.

segments.title: Theories and closing thoughts on the case
segments.summary: Discussion of suicide, espionage and murder theories, a disputed witness account, and the reflection that the case remains unsolved.

segments.title: Listener mail on New Jersey accents
segments.summary: Listener Chris from New Jersey asks about regional accents; the hosts discuss New Jersey speech patterns and pork roll.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give social media and contact information.
